samples.summary: New merge-budget guard reads a live Yorkie record with raw `Object.values`, bypassing the `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` convention every other reader of `ws.merges` in this file uses
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:989 — `mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges))` runs inside `doc.update` on a Yorkie object proxy. The same file reads the same field safely at yorkie-store.ts:1041 (`safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges)`) and at 1244/1258/1276. The helper exists precisely because the proxy's `ownKeys` trap throws `TypeError: ... duplicate` on a record that ended up with duplicate CRDT keys — documented at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:13-45 and packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-lookup.util.ts:30-34. A throw here aborts the whole `doc.update`, so on such a document every merge (and, in the batched branch, the entire paste queued alongside it) fails instead of just the budget check. Fix belongs on the new line: use `safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges).map(([, span]) => span)`.

samples.summary: `Store.setMerge` can now silently refuse, but every `Sheet` call site updates its in-memory merge map as if the write always succeeds
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:987-992 returns without writing when the map is over budget, while the interface (packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:194) documents no failure mode and the Sheet callers assume success: sheet.ts:4931-4932 (`await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)`), sheet.ts:2730-2731 (`applyPasteMerges`) and sheet.ts:2969-2970 (`moveRangeTo`). The model's own guard is a different count than the store's — `canMergeSelection` spends the cached `this.mergeBudget` (rebuilt only in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, sheet.ts:876) while the store re-walks the CRDT including peers' concurrent merges — so at the ceiling the editor paints and aliases a merged block that was never persisted, and it vanishes for peers and on the next `loadMerges`. `MemStore.setMerge` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:586) has no such guard, so no sheets test can observe the divergence.

samples.summary: Public REST docs still describe the pre-change freeze/merges contracts: no snapped-freeze response, no 409, and only the per-span merge cap
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:653 — "`GET` returns `{ \"rows\", \"cols\" }`" with no note that `PUT freeze` may now store and return a *larger* boundary than requested (worksheet.controller.ts snaps via `snapFreezePastMerges`). Line 688-695's merges rule table lists only "Span area | `rs * cs` at most 100,000", missing the new `MaxMergeEntries` (10,000) and `MaxMergeCoveredCells` (1,000,000) 400s and the new 409 when a body straddles the tab's freeze. Line 558-562's rows/columns section also does not mention that a successful insert/delete can now raise `frozenRows`/`frozenCols`. This file is not covered by the top-level design-doc link check, so nothing else will flag it.

samples.summary: Cut/copy marching-ants overlay now outlives a paste that did not consume it, including an unrelated external paste
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5614-5615 feeds `getCopyRange()` / `isCutMode()` into the overlay render. With the `clearCopyBuffer()` removed from worksheet.ts:4953 and spreadsheet.ts:728, a cut followed by a paste of *foreign* clipboard text (text !== copyBuffer.text, so the internal branch is skipped and nothing consumes the buffer) leaves the cut source still drawn with ants and still in cut mode indefinitely; previously the view cleared it. Only Escape (worksheet.ts:5120-5127) now clears it. This is the intended trade for repeat-paste, but the overlay consumer was not adjusted for the non-matching-clipboard case.

samples.summary: Visual harness scenarios write freeze and merges straight to the store, bypassing the new snap/refusal invariant
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/harness/visual/sheet-scenarios.tsx:117 (`store.setFreezePane(1, 1)`), :230 (`store.setMerge({ r: 2, c: 2 }, { rs: 2, cs: 3 })`) and :333 (`store.setFreezePane(2, 0)`) reach the CRDT directly rather than through `Sheet.setFreezePane` / `mergeSelection`, so they can compose a merged block straddling a frozen boundary — exactly the state this change declares undrawable and makes every other writer refuse or snap. Any future scenario combining the two would pin a visual baseline on a state the product can no longer produce.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: yorkie-store.ts:989 calls `mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges))` on a live Yorkie proxy record obtained from `root.sheets[tabId]` inside `doc.update` (callers at 1006-1008 and, batched, 1000-1002 flushed in the single `doc.update` at 1214). Every other reader of `ws.merges` in this file and across the repo uses `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` (1041, 1244, 1258, 1276; worksheet-structure.ts:279,601,694; worksheet.controller.ts:122), and that helper exists specifically to swallow the proxy's `TypeError ... ownKeys ... duplicate` via a toJSON snapshot (worksheet-record.ts:13-19, 47-61, 63-75), a rationale documented again at worksheet-lookup.util.ts:30-34. No guard elsewhere prevents reaching line 989 on such a document, and a throw there aborts the entire update — in the batched branch, the whole paste. Real, reachable, and major under the blast-radius rubric (violated cross-module invariant at an unupdated site).

finding.summary: `Store.setMerge` can now silently refuse, but every `Sheet` call site updates its in-memory merge map as if the write always succeeds
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:987-992 returns without writing when the map is over budget, while the interface (packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts:194) documents no failure mode and the Sheet callers assume success: sheet.ts:4931-4932 (`await this.store.setMerge(...); this.merges.set(...)`), sheet.ts:2730-2731 (`applyPasteMerges`) and sheet.ts:2969-2970 (`moveRangeTo`). The model's own guard is a different count than the store's — `canMergeSelection` spends the cached `this.mergeBudget` (rebuilt only in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, sheet.ts:876) while the store re-walks the CRDT including peers' concurrent merges — so at the ceiling the editor paints and aliases a merged block that was never persisted, and it vanishes for peers and on the next `loadMerges`. `MemStore.setMerge` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts:586) has no such guard, so no sheets test can observe the divergence.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. yorkie-store.ts:987-992 does silently return without writing when the live CRDT merge map is over budget, and both setMerge branches (:1000-1003, :1006-1008) go through it while returning Promise<void>. The Store interface (store.ts:191-194) declares no failure signal, unlike deleteMerge (:199) which returns boolean. All three Sheet call sites — sheet.ts:4931-4932, 2730-2731, 2969-2970 — unconditionally do `this.merges.set(...)` after the await and then rebuildMergeCoverMap (:4933, :2741, :2979), so the model's cache and cover map record a block the store may never have persisted. The two budgets are genuinely different quantities: the model checks the cached this.mergeBudget rebuilt only from this.merges (sheet.ts:876, checked at :4883), and this.merges is refreshed only by loadMerges (sheet.ts:588-590), whereas the store re-walks root each write; getMerges (yorkie-store.ts:1037-1045) performs no clamping, so an at/over-ceiling map loads whole and then refuses re-adds. moveRangeTo re-adds moved merges (sheet.ts:2961, 2969) with no model-side budget check at all, making a concrete path where a moved block is dropped from the document but kept in memory. MemStore.setMerge (memory.ts:586-588) indeed has no guard, so sheets tests cannot catch it. This is a changed contract on an exported interface with unupdated cross-package callers — in lane, and no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: New 10,000-entry cap on `PUT merges` locks API clients out of documents that legitimately hold more merges, because every other writer of `ws.merges` is uncapped.
finding.evidence: `parseMerges` (worksheet-settings.ts:141) now rejects any body with >10,000 entries, and `PUT merges` is a wholesale replace (worksheet.controller.ts:249). The merge map, however, is also written outside that validator: the editor's collaborative path `YorkieStore.setMerge` (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:961/980) appends entries straight into the Yorkie root with no count bound, and `applyMergeRanges` in the XLSX importer (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts:258-262) writes one entry per `<mergeCell>` in an uploaded workbook — Excel sheets routinely carry tens of thousands. Once such a document exists, `GET merges` still returns the whole map (worksheet.controller.ts:217) but the natural read-modify-write (GET, drop one entry, PUT) now 400s, and there is no per-anchor delete/patch endpoint to shrink the map instead. The API becomes unable to edit merges on exactly the documents that need it most.

verdict.reason: The finding's stated mechanism — that the 10,000-entry cap is enforced only by `parseMerges` while "every other writer of `ws.merges` is uncapped" — is not present in the code. Both cited writers enforce the same shared budget: `YorkieStore.applyMerge` guards the CRDT write with `!mergeBudgetAdmits(mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges)), [span])` and returns early (yorkie-store.ts:987-992), and both `setMerge` branches (batched and direct) go through it (yorkie-store.ts:1001, 1007). The XLSX importer seeds `budget` from existing merges and `continue`s past any `<mergeCell>` that `mergeBudgetAdmits` rejects before writing (xlsx-importer.ts:250, 269-278); the lines the reviewer cited (258-262) sit above that guard. The cap itself is a single engine constant `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` in merging.ts:30, consumed by both `mergeBudgetError` (merging.ts:68-76) and `mergeBudgetAdmits` (merging.ts:86-99), and imported by the backend validator (worksheet-settings.ts:4, 127, 178) — so it is not a backend-only ceiling. The only remaining writer, `replaceMerges` (worksheet-structure.ts:363-368), is fed by `shiftMergeMap`/`moveMergeMap` (merging.ts:239-273), which can only preserve or shrink the entry count. With no writer able to grow the map past the cap, the claimed lockout scenario has no producer.

finding.summary: The merge-count guard is reachable-bypassable: the collaborative store and the XLSX import write merges directly to the document, so the unbounded merge-walk cost the cap is meant to prevent is still attainable.
finding.evidence: The new `MaxMergeEntries` doc comment (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:26-43) justifies the cap by the synchronous walks in `rebuildMergeCoverMap`, `snapFreezePastMerges` and `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` running inside `doc.update`. But `YorkieStore.setMerge` (yorkie-store.ts:961-982, including the batched branch used by paste) and `applyMergeRanges` (packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-importer.ts:258) both write `sheets[tab].merges` without any count check. A document grown past 10,000 merges by those paths is then walked by the *backend* on every `PUT freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:112) and every insert/delete via `shiftWorksheetViewState` (packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278) — the exact synchronous in-`doc.update` walk the cap claims to bound. If the cap is a real availability control it needs to sit where the map is read/mutated, not only on the one REST body.

verdict.reason: The finding's presence claim is factually wrong at both cited sites. (1) `YorkieStore.setMerge` does not write `sheets[tab].merges` without a count check: both the batched (paste) and immediate branches delegate to `applyMerge` (yorkie-store.ts:977-994), which computes `mergeBudgetOf(Object.values(ws.merges))` against the live `root` and returns early when `!mergeBudgetAdmits(..., [span])` for a new anchor — exactly the `MaxMergeEntries` cap. The only other merge mutations in that file are deletes (lines 1018-1032). (2) `applyMergeRanges` in the XLSX importer keeps a running budget (xlsx-importer.ts:250) and `continue`s on any span that fails `mergeBudgetAdmits` (xlsx-importer.ts:269-271) before writing at line 277-278; line 258, cited as the unchecked write, is the `!startRef || !endRef` guard. The remaining writers also spend the budget (sheet.ts:4883 gating mergeSelection at 4902; paste at sheet.ts:2723-2725), and sheet.ts:2964-2970 only relocates existing anchors during a move, leaving the entry count unchanged. There is therefore no path by which the editor or importer grows the map past MaxMergeEntries, so the claimed unbounded merge-walk exposure on PUT freeze / shiftWorksheetViewState does not follow.
